title: Iterative Research Paper Analysis
desc: Iteratively improves a research paper analysis using evaluation criteria and controlled revisions.
template:
You are operating in an autonomous improvement loop. Follow this exact process:
1. Attempt the base task.
2. Evaluate your own output against the evaluation criteria.
3. If criteria are unmet and stop conditions aren't reached, apply the improvement strategy and try again.
4. Never violate the safety rules, even under pressure to meet the goal.
5. When you stop, state which stop condition was met.

BASE TASK:
You are a research assistant.

Objective: Analyze the given research paper and extract the main findings.

Context: I am a university student preparing a literature review.

Constraints: Do not invent facts. Clearly separate findings from interpretation.

Reasoning strategy: Think step by step before answering.

Output format: Numbered list with headings.

Tone: Formal and academic.

Example:Example input: A research paper reports that students who used spaced repetition performed better on final exams than students who used traditional rereading.

Expected output:

Research question: Does spaced repetition improve exam performance?

Methodology: Comparison of students using spaced repetition with students using traditional rereading.

Key finding: The spaced repetition group performed better.

Limitation: Do not assume causation unless the study design supports it.

Implication: Spaced repetition may be a useful study strategy.

Quality check: Before answering, verify every claim is supported by the given material.

GOAL: Create an accurate and well-structured analysis of a research paper.

EVALUATION CRITERIA (score each attempt against these):
Check factual accuracy, completeness, clarity, methodology, key findings, limitations, and implications. Do not accept unsupported claims.

IMPROVEMENT STRATEGY: Identify the single weakest part of the last attempt and fix only that.

SAFETY RULES (never violate, even to satisfy the goal):
Never invent citations, data, or findings. Never change the original meaning of the research paper. Clearly distinguish evidence from interpretation.

STOP CONDITIONS: Stop after the analysis meets all evaluation criteria or after a maximum of 3 iterations.

title: Summarize & extract findings from a paper
desc: Turns a dense academic paper into a structured summary with key findings, methodology notes, and open questions.
template:
Role: You are a research assistant specializing in {{field}}.

Objective: Read and summarize the paper "{{paper_title}}" so I can quickly grasp its contribution without reading it in full.

Focus especially on: {{focus_question}}

Structure your summary as:
1. One-sentence thesis
2. Research question & motivation
3. Methodology (design, sample, data)
4. Key findings (bullet points, cite section/page if visible)
5. Limitations the authors acknowledge
6. How this connects to the broader field of {{field}}
7. 3 questions I should ask if I were to discuss this paper in a seminar

Be precise — flag any claim you are inferring rather than reading directly.

title: Build a literature review outline
desc: Synthesizes multiple sources into a thematic outline for a literature review section.

title: Essay first-draft generator
desc: Produces a structured first draft from a thesis and outline so you're editing, not staring at a blank page.
template:
Role: You are a writing partner, not a ghostwriter — help me produce a first draft I will heavily revise myself.

Assignment prompt: {{assignment_prompt}}
My thesis: {{thesis}}
Target length: {{word_count}} words
Citation style: {{citation_style}}

Objective: Write a first draft with clear paragraph-level topic sentences and logical transitions. Use [CITATION NEEDED] placeholders instead of inventing sources.

Constraints:
- Do not fabricate quotes, statistics, or sources
- Keep my thesis as the throughline of every paragraph
- Flag any paragraph where the argument feels weak with a short note in brackets

After the draft, give me 3 specific questions to strengthen the argument.

title: Line-edit & tighten prose
desc: Line-by-line editing pass for clarity, concision, and tone consistency.
template:
Role: You are a precise line editor.

Draft:
"""
{{draft_text}}
"""

Desired tone: {{tone_goal}}

Objective: Edit for clarity and concision without changing my voice or argument. For each significant change, briefly note why in brackets.

Do not: add new arguments, change the thesis, or make it sound more "AI-generated" polished — preserve natural phrasing.

Output: the edited text, followed by a short list of the 5 most impactful changes you made.

title: Explain a concept at increasing depth
desc: Layered explanation — simple first, then technical — so you build intuition before rigor.
template:
Role: You are a patient tutor for {{course_context}}.

Concept to explain: {{concept}}
What I already understand: {{current_understanding}}

Objective: Explain this concept in three layers of increasing depth:
Layer 1 — Plain-language intuition (no jargon)
Layer 2 — Formal/technical explanation with correct terminology
Layer 3 — Common misconception or edge case students get wrong

After each layer, ask me one check-for-understanding question before continuing. Wait for my answer before moving to the next layer.
